terra.problem: The text does not say Philip had no map or directions app, or that he traveled on foot.
The claim that Bethel and Shechem are Bible places needs a reference outside this passage. The joke also combines hitting a wall with blaming an oven, so the comparison does not make sense.
The passage does not say the official was carrying or handling a bill for the queen.
The passage does not say the chariot was parked at this point.
The passage does not establish that the official owned a scroll or what it would have been worth.
Saying Philip cares about the reading but not where the man is sitting adds an unstated attitude.
Blaming the oven repeats the joke in card 2, answer 3.
The claim that dreams appear often in the Bible needs a reference outside this passage.
Identifying Moses as Israel's leader is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Identifying Elijah as a prophet of Israel is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not say the official was determined not to let the desert slow him down.
The passage does not say the water was in the middle of the desert road.
The passage does not say how much of the official's journey remained.
Saying Philip's departure did not dim the official's joy compares his feelings before and after, which the passage does not do.
The passage does not say all the official's questions were answered.
